_about: Industry facet — WHOSE problem the deployment solves. The industry of the ADOPTING organisation, never the publisher, the AI vendor or the platform provider. 18 entries: 7 priority, 8 standard, 3 record_only.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation is a bank, insurer, capital-markets firm, payments company, asset manager or fintech — its business IS financial services.
exclusions: the finance department of a non-financial company
a manufacturer's treasury team
corporate FP&A
entries.disambiguation: Decided by what the ORGANISATION is, not what the task is. A retailer automating invoice matching is retail-cpg + finance-accounting, not this value.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation is a care provider, payer, pharmaceutical or biotech company, medical-device maker or clinical research organisation.
exclusions: a corporate employee-wellbeing programme at a non-healthcare employer
consumer fitness apps with no clinical context
entries.disambiguation: A pharmaceutical company optimising a production line is healthcare-life-sciences (industry) + production-operations (function), not manufacturing-industrial.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation sells goods to consumers, or makes consumer-packaged goods: retailers, e-commerce, grocery, consumer brands.
exclusions: a B2B industrial distributor with no consumer channel
a marketplace platform whose own business is software
entries.disambiguation: Retail-media work is retail-cpg (industry) + marketing (function). The word 'retail' never implies a business function on its own.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation makes physical things — discrete or process manufacturing, industrial equipment, automotive, chemicals, electronics.
exclusions: a software firm that 'manufactures' nothing physical
a pharma company's production line (that is healthcare-life-sciences)
entries.disambiguation: Against the production-operations FUNCTION: this value says the organisation makes things; production-operations says the work happens in the production function, in any industry.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation sells expertise as its product: law firms, consultancies, accounting firms, agencies, architecture and engineering practices.
exclusions: an in-house legal department at a non-services company
an internal consulting team
entries.disambiguation: A law FIRM using AI is professional-services. In-house legal at a manufacturer is manufacturing-industrial + legal-risk-compliance.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation is a government body, agency, defence organisation, municipality or civic service provider.
exclusions: a private contractor selling to government
a state-owned commercial bank (that is financial-services-insurance)
entries.disambiguation: The adopter must be the public body. A vendor's case study about serving an agency takes the agency's industry, not the vendor's.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation is a school, university, college, education provider or research institute.
exclusions: corporate training inside a non-education employer
employee upskilling programmes
entries.disambiguation: Against the training-enablement FUNCTION: a university is education-research; a bank running staff upskilling is financial-services-insurance + training-enablement.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation generates or distributes energy, operates utilities, or extracts natural resources: power, oil and gas, mining, water.
exclusions: a manufacturer's internal energy-efficiency project
a bank financing renewables
entries.disambiguation: The organisation's own business must be energy, utilities or resources; funding or consuming energy does not qualify.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation moves goods or people: carriers, freight operators, third-party logistics, ports, rail, mobility providers.
exclusions: a retailer's internal supply-chain team (that is retail-cpg + supply-chain-operations)
an airline (that is travel-hospitality)
entries.disambiguation: Against supply-chain-operations (function): this value is for organisations whose BUSINESS is moving things; the function is the work, in any industry.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation grows, farms, fishes or produces food and agricultural products.
exclusions: a grocery retailer (that is retail-cpg)
a restaurant chain (that is travel-hospitality)
entries.disambiguation: Ends where the product reaches a retailer or a restaurant.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation develops, builds, manages or transacts property: architecture, engineering and construction, property management, real-estate services.
exclusions: a corporate facilities team inside another industry (that is facilities-workplace)
a mortgage lender (that is financial-services-insurance)
entries.disambiguation: Against facilities-workplace (function): this value is the property business itself; the function is running a workplace, in any industry.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation is an airline, hotel, restaurant group, cruise line, travel platform or venue operator.
exclusions: corporate travel management inside another industry
a food producer (that is agriculture-food)
entries.disambiguation: The guest-facing operator qualifies; a company that merely buys travel does not.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation publishes, broadcasts, produces or distributes content: publishers, studios, streaming services, gaming, music, sports.
exclusions: a brand's content-marketing team (that is marketing)
a technology company that hosts media
entries.disambiguation: Against content-generation (use case): this value is who the adopter is; the use case is what the AI does, in any industry.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation operates communications networks or services: mobile and fixed carriers, cable, satellite, network operators.
exclusions: an enterprise IT network team (that is it-infrastructure)
a cloud provider (that is technology-software)
entries.disambiguation: The organisation must sell connectivity; operating an internal network does not qualify.

entries.definition: The adopting organisation is a charity, NGO, foundation, humanitarian or social-impact organisation.
exclusions: a company's corporate-social-responsibility programme
a public agency (that is public-sector-government)
entries.disambiguation: A corporate CSR initiative keeps the company's own industry.

entries.definition: The ADOPTING organisation itself sells software, hardware or technology services. Recorded when genuinely evidenced, never actively sought.
exclusions: the PUBLISHER of the article
the AI vendor whose model is used
the cloud, framework or hosting provider
the fact that the piece appears on a technology website
any organisation that merely uses software
entries.disambiguation: record_only by design. A customer case published by an AI vendor takes the CUSTOMER's industry: an OpenAI story about a hospital is healthcare-life-sciences. Otherwise this value becomes the dumping ground for every vendor case study.

entries.definition: The deployment is genuinely horizontal, or is documented across multiple named industries, so no single industry describes it.
positive_terms: customers in banking, retail and healthcare
exclusions: a tool that COULD theoretically be used broadly
a generic reusable component with one named adopter
an unknown industry (that is other-unclear)
entries.disambiguation: record_only, target_min 0. Counted separately; it never satisfies or reduces the gap of any concrete industry and never launches a gap-filling lane of its own.

entries.definition: The source discusses the adopting organisation but supports no vocabulary value — the industry cannot be placed from the evidence available.
exclusions: a horizontal deployment (that is cross-industry)
an axis that does not apply at all (record not_applicable in unresolved[])
entries.disambiguation: The single sentinel shared by all three axes, and the only slug exempt from cross-axis disjointness. other-unclear alone never satisfies the Domain Applications non-trivial requirement.
